flashcard_questions.q: Which project does Snowball argue will reduce the animals’ labour?
Which Soviet policy does Snowball’s position mirror?
Which rival Soviet policy does Napoleon’s position mirror?
Which class does Mollie the white mare represent?
Why does Orwell present Mollie as unsympathetic?
flashcard_questions.a: She cares more about her own comfort than about collective justice.

flashcard_questions.q: Which signal does Napoleon use to launch his coup against Snowball?
How many dogs burst into the barn to drive Snowball out?
Which secret police force do those dogs represent?
When was Trotsky exiled from the Soviet Union?
What does Napoleon abolish to end democratic debate on the farm?
What word does Squealer use to excuse Napoleon’s earlier opposition?
Which relic does Napoleon put on display for weekly viewing?
Which real Soviet practice does that display parallel?
flashcard_questions.a: Lenin’s embalmed body in the Red Square mausoleum.

flashcard_questions.q: Which second motto does Boxer adopt after Snowball is expelled?

flashcard_questions.a: Biased or misleading information used to promote a political cause.

notes: 15 cards: 5 allegory mappings (Snowball, Napoleon, Mollie, the dogs, the skull), 5 plot-detail fronts (the windmill, the whimper, nine dogs, the Sunday meetings, ‘tactics’), 2 context facts (1929 exile, Lenin’s mausoleum), 1 quotation-recall (Boxer’s motto), 1 character-motive card (Mollie), 1 term-to-definition (propaganda). ‘Totalitarian’, ‘hierarchy’ and ‘cult of personality’ dropped as glossary restatements; Squealer’s ‘loyalty and obedience’ line cut because the only honest card would be an enumeration. All quotations verbatim from the lesson content.
